name: Aripiprazole
drug_class: Atypical antipsychotic; dopamine D2 partial agonist
route_note: Oral tablets, ODT or solution once daily; IM long-acting injections monthly or every 2 months (aripiprazole lauroxil every 1–2 months).

discovery.by: Yasuo Oshiro, Tetsuro Kikuchi and colleagues (Otsuka)
discovery.note: Developed from a programme seeking dopamine autoreceptor agonists, yielding a quinolinone with partial D2 agonism.

tagline: First dopamine partial agonist antipsychotic, with a low metabolic burden
summary: Aripiprazole is a dopamine D2 partial agonist antipsychotic, discovered by Otsuka. It stabilises dopamine signalling rather than blocking it fully, and is used for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, adjunctive treatment of depression, irritability in autism and Tourette syndrome. It became one of the best-selling drugs in the US.
mechanism: As a partial agonist at D2 receptors, aripiprazole reduces signalling where dopamine is excessive (mesolimbic pathway) and provides some stimulation where it is deficient, acting as a 'dopamine system stabiliser'. It is also a 5-HT1A partial agonist and 5-HT2A antagonist.
This profile is associated with little prolactin elevation and relatively low metabolic risk, but akathisia is common, and the dopamine agonism is linked to impulse-control problems.
uses: Acute and maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder
Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder
Agitation in schizophrenia or bipolar mania (IM)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Abilify (Otsuka/Bristol-Myers Squibb) is approved for schizophrenia in November 2002.

history.title: Bipolar mania
history.detail: Aripiprazole is approved for acute mania.

history.title: Adjunctive depression
history.detail: It becomes the first antipsychotic approved as an add-on for major depression.

history.title: Abilify Maintena
history.detail: The monthly long-acting injection is approved.

history.title: Generics and Aristada
history.detail: Generic aripiprazole launches in the US; Alkermes' aripiprazole lauroxil is approved.

history.title: Impulse-control warning
history.detail: The FDA warns of compulsive gambling, shopping, eating and sexual behaviour.

history.title: Abilify MyCite
history.detail: The first drug with an ingestible sensor to track ingestion is approved.

history.title: Abilify Asimtufii
history.detail: A two-monthly long-acting injection is approved.

safety.boxed_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; not approved for this use. Suicidal thoughts and behaviours with antidepressant use in young people (where approved for depression).

facts: Aripiprazole was the first marketed dopamine partial agonist antipsychotic; brexpiprazole and cariprazine followed.
